about: Where a fetched source's cached copy lands (INTEGRATIONS-2a). The canonical id is the id trimmed of ASCII whitespace. An issue key is lowercased. A URL loses one leading http:// or https:// in any case, its host (everything before the first /, ? or #) is ASCII-lowercased, and trailing / go; path case, query and fragment stay part of the identity. An issue lands at sources/issues/<canonical>.md. A web page lands at sources/web/<readable>-<suffix>.md: readable is the canonical id with every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] turned into -, runs of - collapsed, leading - and . and trailing - trimmed, lowercased, cut to 64 characters and trimmed of trailing - again; suffix is the first 12 hex characters of sha256("cerebro-source-cache-v1\0web\0" + canonical). With nothing readable left the file is sources/web/<suffix>.md. Replayed by source_slugs_replay_the_shared_cases in src-tauri/src/mcp.rs and by src/engine/ingest.test.ts, which both also hold that distinct canonical ids never share a path. `why` is for the reader.

cases.why: An issue's path is the one it has had since M8.2.
Whitespace around an id is not part of it.
Scheme case, host case and a trailing slash are spelling, not identity.
Path case is identity: a case-sensitive server serves two pages.
A fragment is identity: in a single-page app it is the page.
Runs of - collapse. The old twins disagreed here: a.test-a--b against a.test-a-b.
Confluence's +-+, where the old twins wrote release---q3-plan and release-q3-plan, so the Inbox never found the copy.
This page and the next shared one file under the old 80-character cut, and the second fetch overwrote the first.
The same readable half, a different suffix: two files.
Non-ASCII never reaches a file name, and no Unicode class has to mean the same thing in both twins.
Nothing readable left: the suffix alone names the file.
The host ends at the first /, ? or #, and only the host is lowercased.
A file name never starts with a dot: the scan hides dotfiles and the note writers refuse them.
